about: Viña Zorzal is the project of the Sanz brothers, Xabi, Iñaki and Mikel, in Corella in southern Navarra. Their father Antonio began making his own wines in 1989 after a lifetime in the trade, and in 2007 the brothers founded Viña Zorzal, turning away from volume toward small-lot wines that rescue Navarra’s native varieties. Their discovery of old, abandoned Garnacha vineyards in the hills of Fitero shifted the winery toward single-plot wines that speak of where they grow.

This white comes from organically farmed, dry-farmed Garnacha Blanca on stony sedimentary soils around Corella, picked by hand. The free-run juice is drawn off after about twelve hours on the skins and fermented with native yeasts. The wine then rests six months on its lees in a mix of concrete tank, foudre and 500-litre barrels, and is bottled unfined and unfiltered with only a moderate dose of sulphur. About 1,700 cases were made in 2022.

Garnacha Blanca is the white mutation of Garnacha, long grown in the Ebro valley but rarely bottled on its own. In Zorzal’s hands it is a dry, medium-bodied white of citrus, peach, apricot and a soft mineral edge, its freshness kept by the stony ground and the absence of new oak. Recent vintages have drawn strong praise, with Wine Advocate scoring the 2023 and 2024 at 93 points.
facts: 6 months on the lees in concrete, foudre and 500 L barrels
